relationships.subject: Triptans
relationships.evidence_quote: Triptans target mainly the 5-HT1B and 5-HT1D receptor subtypes, located at meningeal vessels but also within the trigeminal nerve endings and trigeminal nucleus and suppresses the release of CGRP [34, 35].

relationships.subject: Chronic migraine
relationships.evidence_quote: NR suffered significantly more often from CM than SR (NR n = 24/26, 92% vs. SR n = 15/29, 52%; p = 0.001).

relationships.subject: Depression
relationships.evidence_quote: NR suffered significantly more often from concomitant depression than SR (NR n = 17/26, 65% vs. SR n = 8/29, 28%; p = 0.005)

key_findings: 11% of treatment-resistant migraine patients were super-responders and 10% non-responders to CGRP(-R) mAbs.
Non-responders had more chronic migraine, medication overuse headache and depression; super-responders had better triptan response and more vomiting.
